correctness.rationale: A highest-priority vertex is always a local maximum, and precisely its deleted-matching partner can be another; it is another exactly when second highest. This gives the exact mutually exclusive singleton and pair probabilities. The posterior is uniform over all matching completions because singleton likelihoods are constant and each observed pair supplies only membership information. Relabelling symmetry upgrades the Bayes upper bound to the exact minimax value. Unseen-coupon factorial moments converge to Poisson in the critical window; negative indicator covariance controls the subcritical region. The identity and boundaries were also checked by 416 standalone exact-rational assertions, including exhaustive permutations through six labels. Tests support, but do not prove, the asymptotics.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The inferred i.i.d. coupon categories are *unobserved matched pairs*. Even when one edge is unseen, the perfect-matching completion is unique; when u are unseen, there are (2u−1)!! completions. This posterior correction produces e^(−lambda)cosh(sqrt(2lambda)), which is not the classical full-collection probability e^(−lambda). The strongest compared graph identification results do not imply this correction.

originality.rationale: The assessed statement is the exact minimax recovery law and nonstandard hyperbolic-cosine critical success profile for the unknown deleted perfect matching seen only through local maxima. The prior random-labeling, coupon-collection and covariance-based graph-identification statements do not entail that observation channel or exact posterior. Search noncoverage is treated as uncertain historical evidence, not as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The dense hidden perfect-matching family is a natural extremal test of inference from graph-local peaks. A two-peak observation reveals a specific missing edge, whereas singleton peaks reveal no matching information. The exact minimax probability includes unavoidable ambiguity among unseen pairs and yields a sharp n²log n sampling transition with a nonclassical, explicitly evaluable recovery curve; this quantifies a genuine information-theoretic obstacle and an attaining estimator.
